verify.cmd: node -e 'const fs=require("fs");const fail=(m)=>{console.error(m);process.exit(1)};const strip=(s)=>s.replace(/\/\*[\s\S]*?\*\//g,"").replace(/^\s*\/\/.*$/gm,"");const mw=fs.readFileSync("lib/calendar/month-window.ts","utf8");const page=fs.readFileSync("app/(main)/spaces/[slug]/settings/calendar/page.tsx","utf8");const fwd=Number((mw.match(/OPERATOR_HORIZON_FORWARD_MONTHS\s*=\s*(\d+)/)||[])[1]);if(!(fwd>=13))fail("the operator entry window reaches "+fwd+" months forward, so a Space whose season runs a full year ahead loses its far dates on List and Workflow again: those two views derive from ONE server read and never page");if(!/entryWindow:\s*horizon/.test(strip(page))||!/horizon\s*=\s*operatorHorizonWindow\(now\)/.test(strip(page)))fail("the operator Calendar tab no longer anchors its entry window on today, so List and Workflow are bounded by something other than the horizon the tests pin");if(/yearHorizonWindow/.test(strip(mw)+strip(page)))fail("the calendar-year window is back in live code: it spanned January to January of the viewers own year and hid 98 of Royal Temples 128 dates while the month grid showed them");'
verify.note: Measures the consequence an owner meets (a date a year out survives the window the two derived views read) rather than the presence of a helper, per HYG-108. The forward span is read out of the shipped constant and arithmetic-checked, the page is checked to be wired to it, and the removed calendar-year window is checked not to have come back. The operator entry window now lives in the console route (the public tab is the visitor calendar, LIVE-1704); the probe reads it there.
